summary: The author asked why no data modelling was visible in the first sandbox and whether a data model readable by people and machines, navigable across abstraction levels and refinement stages and tied to metadata and loading patterns, could replace PowerDesigner's role with open-source or self-built parts.
verbatim: I've been thinking. We have a nice schematic of what we do. We just did our first trial case. That got me wondering. We didn't do any data modelling. At least not explicitly or visibly. Why is this important? The data model (conceptual, logical, technical) is a means of communication and of tracking the big picture for humans. Furthermore if we do the data modelling correctly we can do data warehouse automation, and use templates to generate deterministic loading patterns. Following up on this, is there a way to create data models that are both readable to humans and machines, like in ASCII art or something? We should be able to navigate through the data model, go from conceptual to logical to technical, and through the different stages of refinement, raw, datavault, dimensional model. It should be navigable for both humans and the agentic layer. The data model should be connected to meta data, so that we can retrieve meaning, but also loading patterns etc. I have been using SAP PowerDesigner at work, where they have created a complete suite around that generates all code. This is actually quite powerful, but SAP PowerDesigner is a nightmare to navigate through and it carries a lot of unnecesarry ballast. Maybe we can do better. I still prefer everything open source, or created by you. Your thoughts on this?
notes: task_type planning rather than modelling: the subject is how modelling would be done in the framework, and no data asset was touched.
